notes.title: A thanks, and Patch 0.3.1!
notes.content: [p]It's been an eventful weekend after the EA launch, and I wanted to just say thanks again for everyone who took the risk on a small solo dev and purchased the game! We've managed to amass enough reviews to hit Very Positive, which is absolutely incredible. I can't thank you all enough for your support. I truly never thought I'd reach that milestone with this project.[/p][p][/p][p]I've spent most of the weekend fixing bugs and quality of life issues that you've all been diligently reporting. I particularly appreciate all the patience in dealing with those lategame run-ending softlocks. The ingame bug reports have helped a ton, as they give me a copy of your character in addition to the error logs. This makes it much easier for me to hunt things down![/p][p][/p][p]Now that the game is stabilizing, I wanted to release a small chunk of content early as my way of saying thanks for sticking through the bugs![/p][p][/p][p][b]Arcanist Changes:[/b][/p][p]Compared to the Adventurer and Beastmaster, the Arcanist isn't in quite as good of a spot as I'd like. The Adventurer has powerful lategame scaling with Block, Resists, Spirit, and the Ascalon line. The Beastmaster can scale heavily with Minion Monster Level as well. Arcanist only really has Mana as a lategame endless scaler. This patch, focusing on the Conjuror tree, aims to help with that a bit. More changes are forthcoming, of course![/p][list][*][p]Added Tempest Shield, Hoary Shield, and Inferno Shield to the Conjuror tree[/p][/*][*][p]Each of these adds 8% of their matching elemental resistance per skill point as long as you have the matching Conjuror Elemental equipped,[/p][p]Hoarder of the Primordial now causes you to gain 7% increased damage for your Elemental skills per 5 points of uncapped total Elemental Resistance[/p][/*][*][p]The Elemental Skills have had their scaling improved, they now scale their attack rate with CDR, for example[/p][/*][*][p]Arguably a bug fix, but re-summoning an Elemental does not reset its attack cooldown. This increases their DPS substantially if you're using autocast[/p][/*][/list][p] [b]New Content:[/b] [/p][list][*][p]Added one new unique item. Perhaps some Discord community members will find the suggestion familiar![/p][/*][*][p]Added a new endgame crafting system. Good luck to all of you item hunters![/p][/*][/list][p] [b]Fixes and Changes:[/b] [/p][list][*][p]Added some additional safety checks around crafting, to hopefully resolve the crafter lockout issues[/p][/*][*][p]Added some hints to the more elusive conditional uniques. Happy hunting![/p][/*][*][p]Kinetic Blades will no longer gain negative damage from negative resists if you're using those scaling tree nodes[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug with the Avatar of the Hunt Lunar Cry ability[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed 2 buff bugs that may have been causing odd behavior[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed some memory issues with Avatar of Inevitability[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug where Memory Crystals found from the Gambler would not have mods[/p][/*][*][p]The Shrines of Indifference and Charity now are easier to select on the controller[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the gold display on a few crafting windows[/p][/*][*][p]Made a supremely rare unique 3x more common. I doubt this will make much of a difference, but best of luck![/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug where achievements requiring you to enter anomalies were not tracking[/p][/*][*][p]Removed the -Scroll Speed Cursed Shrine outcome, as it was causing some strange side effects[/p][/*][*][p]Improved the egress location for Challenge events in the Kraken arena[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where Depth would not reset on game over if you lost your connection to Steam[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where secret areas could fail to generate an ending if they were meant to spawn a boss[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug where the Spooky Warden's animal trains would sometimes "stick" when entering the real Warden boss fight[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Don't Die, Collect Loot has Entered Early Access!
notes.content:
[h3][b]Don't Die, Collect Loot is now available in Early Access![/b] [/h3][p][/p][previewyoutube="IvKzOe7IRro;full"][/previewyoutube][p]I’ve been building this project solo, and the journey continues with you on today's launch. Early Access is where your feedback matters most, helping shape everything still to come. To kick things off, here’s what you’ll find in the Early Access launch of the game that I've been working on:[/p][p][/p][h3]✨New Skills[/h3][p]Expand the power of the Adventurer, Arcanist, and Beastmaster with new abilities and massive skill tree updates. There are now hundreds of nodes to choose from, providing unique and powerful upgrades to a plethora of new attacks. Even the Exploration tree has received a complete overhaul and expansion! Underperforming skills and abilities have been updated as well, based on all of your feedback from the demo.[/p][p][/p][h3]🌊Explore the Aqueduct[/h3][p]Discover the ruins of humanity's past progress in the new Aqueduct zone! This area features an entire cast of new enemies, including three new devious bosses. All of this content is also added to Don't Die, Collect Loot's endgame: The Endless Nightmare. This endgame allows for infinite progression and exploration, allowing you to customize your experience to your playstyle! Casual and hardcore gamers alike will have plenty to enjoy.[/p][p][/p][h3]📿 Items Galore[/h3][p]Tons of new unique items, item bases, and other loot have been added to the game. The ability to socket custom craft-able memories into items has been added as well. The possibilities are virtually endless, and player power can skyrocket in unique and ridiculous ways. Tailor your build to your power fantasy![/p][p][/p][h3]🎟️Random Events[/h3][p]The areas of Don't Die, Collect Loot are now full of random, and sometimes absurd, events! Battle ancient eldritch entities who just happen to have decided to pay you a visit. Locate weird, secret areas and perhaps discover the secret of the Abyss. Face off against unique boss fights and bullet hell survival encounters in the all-new Challenge Mode! notes.title: Untitled
notes.content:
Note: As this demo is also being used to test game balance and fun, nothing that happens is set in stone. Don't like something I changed? Let me know!

[h1]Nightmare Scaling Updates[/h1]
With the fixes to monster life, Nightmare runs go deeper than ever before. I love that everyone is having a ton of fun playing the game for long sessions, and don't intend to discourage that.

However, I do want to also incentivize play for people who prefer shorter, but more challenging runs as well. These changes are designed to help encourage pushing deeper into the Endless Nightmare's tiers as well.

[h2]NM Unique Drop Rate Scaling[/h2]
Currently the optimal strategy is to pick NM 1-3 and just push as deep into the game as possible. You've probably seen some folks on the news feed pushing to depth 800+ and just raining T0 uniques. This will always be a somewhat viable strategy, but two changes are being made to encourage other playstyles:
The base unique drop quality bonus from Nightmare has quintupled. It just wasn't big enough before. Now higher NM levels are much stronger
The Cursed Shrines that gave flat Unique chance now give 3% Unique Item Drop Chance per Difficulty and Nightmare Level. This means that on NM15, this shrine will give a whopping 45% increased Unique drop rate, giving higher NM runners an incentive to push difficulties

[h2]NM Monster Scaling[/h2]
Nightmare monster levels aren't strongly felt by most builds until very high Nightmare values. I've doubled the effect of Nightmare on monster stats. This is a flat bonus per Nightmare difficulty level, not an exponential one. As always, it's tough to tune this game to every possible build, so let me know how this feels for you!

[h1]Other Patch Notes:[/h1]
[list]
[*] Greatly optimized the Fire Attunement skill
[*] Greatly optimized the cost of Skill Tree Change announcements. You shouldn't see lag when selecting upgrades in-run anymore
[*] Moderately optimized the CPU and memory usage of dropping items
[*] Added two missing Weapon modifiers
[*] Reduced some unnecessary memory usage relating to animations
[*] Added some additional instrumentation around performance in hopes of being able to identify more bottlenecks in the future
[*] Reduced the spawn rate of Divinities in half
[/list]

notes.title: 2.3.19 - The Halls of Glory
notes.content:
[h2]The Halls of Glory[/h2]
2.3.19 adds the demo's most popular feature request! Enter the Hall of Heroes and use the new special transit orb there to enter the Halls of Glory. 

The Halls of Glory features a Memory of Glory opponent that can quite literally never die. Not only is he immortal, but he's also surprisingly helpful! The Memory of Glory will tally all of the damage you deal to him in a 10 second rolling window, and use it to compute your DPS. If you're tired of guessing about your damage from all of the complex skill and item sources, this is the place for you!

That's not all, though. Within the Halls of Glory you'll be able to freely change your equipment and tweak your skill tree, making it incredibly easy to test out build changes. You can even interact with a Skill Selection orb that will let you pick upgrades you'd normally find in a run!

[h2]Game EXE Name Change[/h2]
This isn't exciting, but the change is a little scary. The game is now properly named "Don't Die, Collect Loot" instead of "arpg". The save paths depended on this string originally, and this code has been fixed. If you see any issues with your saves, let me know ASAP!

As a minor side effect, window position and resolution may have reset. Sorry about that, but this should be the only time this happens!

[*] Added the Halls of Glory to the game
[*] Reduced the maximum stacks of Shock, Ignite, Poison, and Chill to 99. Yes, this is probably a nerf on very long boss fights, but your CPU will thank you.

[*] Added commas to various gold value displays to improve readability

[*] Added sound effects for Potion
[*] Fixed a bug causing Beastmaster and Arcanist to not display certain visual effects
[*] Reduced the time to load the game by ~35%
[*] Updated the exe name and icon
[/list]

notes.title: 2.3.16 - New crush system
notes.content:
2.3.16 adds a new crush system. Players sometimes get frustrated over losing a life and being generally disrupted by sudden crush events. Being crushed is essential to the design of Don't Die, Collect Loot, but I also understand that this binary system can be frustrating. This patch adds an experimental system that makes crushes somewhat less disruptive. 

The first time you're crushed, you'll lose half your maximum life, and no mitigation will prevent this. You'll become temporarily invincible and can move freely through obstacles on the screen. Once you re-materialize, you'll be back to normal. Note that re-materializing inside of an obstacle, like a body of water or a house, will immediately trigger a second crush. Be careful!

After your first crush, the second will deal 60% of your maximum life. The third will deal 80%, and the fourth will always kill you. This penalty persists throughout the run, even if you die! You can move back a penalty stage by completing an event, however. For example, if you were crushed twice, the third crush will deal 80% of your life. However, you then interact with the Goddess of Fate at the end of a stage. Your crush penalty will now be 60%, should you be crushed again.

As always I'm looking for feedback! Does this help? Is it dumb? Is it more fun? Let me know!

notes.title: 2.3.12 - Ailments and Skill Multiplier
notes.content:
[list]
[*] Ailments have been reworked. This is part of a multi-step process that will end in adding a number of tools to the Arcanist.
[*] Ignite - Ignite takes 100% of the initial hit damage, snapshots it, and deals it over time
[*] Poison - Poison takes 50% of the initial hit damage, snapshots it, and deals it over time. Additionally, Poison reduces the damage dealt by the target by 5% per stack, capping at 50% reduced. Stacks beyond this point only deal damage
[*] Shock - Shock takes 50% of the initial hit damage, snapshots it, and deals it over time. Shock also causes the target to take 10% increased damage, capping at 50%. Stacks beyond this point only deal damage
[*] Chill - Chill takes 50% of the initial hit damage, snapshots it, and deals it over time. If a target is chilled, its Action Speed is also reduced by 35%. This effect does not scale with stacks. Chilled Ground still only applies the speed reduction
[*] Sources of Skill Damage are now multiplicative with other multipliers. This makes skill tree and ingame upgrades much more powerful. This is generally a buff to every build!
[*] Off-screen monsters no longer process collisions
[*] Some sources of repeated buffs, like the Avatar of Night's "Night's Hunger" effect, have been substantially optimized
[/list]

notes.title: Demo Launch!
notes.content:
[h1]Demo Launch[/h1]

If you're reading this, the demo is live, or about to be. I hope you're all as excited as I am!

The demo features 30+ hours of content, and potentially hundreds of hours of endgame for those who are really into min/maxing and leaderboard climbing. 

Today also marks the start of Don't Die, Collect Loot's first season! The leaderboards have been reset, and all playtest characters have been flagged as "Legacy". Don't despair, you can still play them if you prefer long-term progress, they just won't show up on the seasonal leaderboards.

[h2]Season Features[/h2]

[h3]Shared Stash[/h3]
Characters created as part of the new season now have a shared stash! If you find a cool unique or other item you want to use on an alt, you now can. Simply swap to the other character or create a new one. Items do not have level restrictions, so have fun blasting through the earlygame with your newfound power.

Uniques will now also drop on any character instead of being class-specific drops. However, some are restricted to specific characters. Check out the item info tooltip for more details. Additionally, modifiers that can't apply to a character will appear greyed out when viewed by that character to indicate their lack of effect. For example, a mod that adds Maximum Mana will not work on an Adventurer or Beastmaster.

[h3]Ingame Announcements[/h3]
This season also features an ingame announcement window which appears on the left panel. If you're connected to Steam (and the internet, of course) while playing you'll be able to see the ultra rare items other players have found! Your triumphs may be announced to the world too!

Note that Don't Die, Collect Loot does not have DRM nor does it require you to be online to play. These announcements and the leaderboards are optional features for players who like that sense of community competition and shared celebration. If you don't, we totally understand! Enjoy the game your way!

[h2]Patch Notes[/h2]
We haven't just created a new season, a ton of major changes are now going live too!

[h3]Performance[/h3]
[list]
[*] The main executable is now built with C++ instead of .NET. This speeds up a lot of individual operations and reduces the general file size and memory footprint of the game
[*] Some sources of high memory pressure have been refactored to improve performance
[*] Massively improved end-of-level loot tally performance. Your long runs will now take under a second to tally instead of a minute+
[*] Fixed a major performance bug on <REDACTED> involving burning ground
[/list]

[h3]Keybinds[/h3]
You can now rebind the attack and ability keys! More binding support is coming in the future, so stay tuned

[h3]Skills[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added a new Meteor skill tree node that causes Meteors to strike multiple times when cast. This modifier can also be found on items
[/list]

[h3]Items[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added around 40 new base items. These are designed to generally increase mid and lategame power, especially for the Beastmaster
[*] Added 15 new uniques, some of which are super rare endgame uniques that turn the game on its head!
[*] Increased the drop rate of Tier 3 and Tier 2 uniques by 20% and 10% respectively
[/list]

[h3]Balance[/h3]
[list]
[*] Lord of the Storm avatars no longer double-dip when multiplying the damage gained from your equipment and the tree
[*] Lord of the Storm avatars have had their damage effectiveness reduced from 100% to 25%
[*] Whirlwind's base damage has been upgraded from 1 to 2
[*] Whirlwind's tick rate has been increased by 10% now that the engine can handle the higher proc rates
[*] Avatar of the Hunt now increases its flat and multiplicative damage scaling per Minion Monster Level
[*] Avatar of the Hunt's "Revenge of the Pack" ability now adds flat physical damage per Minion Monster Level instead of per skill point
[*] Avatar of the Hunt's attack speed now scales with Minion Attack Rate
[*] Avatar of the Night now increases its flat and multiplicative damage scaling per Minion Monster Level
[*] The Beastmaster combo skill "Eternal Hunt" now procs on 10% of Minion hits instead of 3% of Minion hits
[*] Increased the base flat damage of all Beastmaster summoned pets (but not tamed pets) by 20%
[*] Ignite now ticks at the proper rate. This means Ignites in general do 10% of the damage they used to. This is technically a bug fix, but it manifests as a massive balance change. This means the player will both die much less frequently to Ignite, but your Ignites will also be much weaker!
[*] Reduced Boss flat life and life scaling on Inferno and Endless Nightmare to account for the above
[*] Significantly increased the damage and difficulty of <REDACTED>, while making its phases much more interesting
[/list]

[h3]Bugfixes and Minor Changes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Many monster abilities have had their graphics overhauled in the interest of visual diversity and clarity
[*] "Be the Lion" has had its multiplier values corrected and now functions properly
[*] You can no longer attack or summon pets while reviving
[*] More skills and minion abilities respect the Attack Opacity slider
[*] Added an additional item rarity tile for T0 uniques

[*] Fixed some issues with minion crit display
[*] The Advice NPC in town has learned a lesson in brevity
[*] Fixed some issues with saving dialogue and quest state
[*] Fixed a bug where Storm Avatars and Shield Projectiles would not function properly on <REDACTED>
[*] Fixed a bug where Adventurer could display an insane Attack Multiplier under certain conditions
[/list]

notes.content:
[h1]Arcanist Pre-release Patch Notes[/h1]

This will be the last major playtest update for a while. I'm still going to continue to add some minor content for a while, primarily in the form of new item bases and unique items, especially for the Arcanist and the Beastmaster. I also have one final special surprise feature in store that I think you'll all really enjoy.

I really want to thank everyone who participated, it's been a humbling and amazing experience. I can't wait to show you all what I have in store for Don't Die, Collect Loot in the near future. In the meantime, tell your friends about all the fun you had!

Once the playtest concludes, all content will be available permanently as a Demo, so don't worry about the game disappearing! As always, I'm also interested in recruiting some Alpha testers to join our community. Existing players who have tested extensively will be automatically invited to this process once the demo drops.


[h2]The Arcanist[/h2]

The Arcanist is now selectable as a playable character. She deals heavy spell damage, and relies on Mana as a resource. 

The Arcanist currently has 3 sub-trees, Pyromancer, Runemaster, and Arcanist.

[h3]Pyromancer[/h3]

Deal heavy Fire damage to foes while scaling Ignite damage

[b]Fireball[/b] - Launch a Fireball at your enemies, which explodes upon impact. Scales heavily with area, more projectiles, and Ignite. Has a low Mana cost and is relatively easy to spam

[b]Meteor[/b] - Summon a Meteor directly onto an enemy or location. Costs a large amount of mana, but deals massive damage. Can be upgraded to either (or both!) summon additional Meteors or leave burning lava pools behind on impact, which Ignite enemies who touch them

[b]This is Fine (Ultimate)[/b] - While active, automatically spreads Ignites to all enemies on the screen while also increasing Ignite damage

[h3]Runemaster[/h3]

Manipulate your Mana supply to deal incredible damage. May require some expertise at the game to utilize properly

[b]Runic Blade[/b] - Swing your shortsword, dealing damage to nearby enemies while draining their lifeforce as Mana. Costs no Mana to use. Runic Blade can be augmented to become larger and deal additional damage based on the Mana you spent to cast your last spell. It can also be upgraded to buff the damage of the next spell you cast based on how much Mana Runic Blade would recovery.

[b]Rune Blast[/b] - Spend all of your Mana to summon a slow-moving orb of pure magical energy. Use the ability a second time to detonate the orb for massive Lightning damage. The more Mana you spend on casting this, the larger the explosion and the more damage it does! Can be upgraded to convert the damage to Fire, or to deal massive Shocks.

[b]Infinity (Ultimate)[/b] - Your Mana pool is doubled and is always full. You always count as having spent all your Mana for Runic Blade and Rune Blast. It's up to you to figure out how to maximize the potential here!

[h3]Conjuror[/h3]

A more passive playstyle focusing on summoning Elementals that fight for you. The Elementals also provide permanent buffs when their skills are equipped on your bar.

[b]Water Attunement[/b] - Conjure up a permanent Water Orb familiar. This provides you a permanent Cold Damage buff while equipped. Use the skill to summon a Water Elemental which focuses on a spread of projectiles. These projectiles can be upgraded in various ways to increase their clear potential.

[b]Fire Attunement[/b] - Conjure up a permanent Fire Orb familiar. This provides you a permanent Fire Damage buff while equipped. Use the skill to summon a Fire Elemental which focuses on a targeted barrage of powerful projectiles. You can upgrade the familiar to increase the power and frequency of the barrage


[h2]Beastmaster[/h2]

The Beastmaster is currently somewhat weaker than the other classes, primarily due to the challenges of scaling pets. The following changes have been made to help, with more coming:

[list]
[*] A number of flat Minion Damage modifiers have been added to the item modifier pool
[*] The Whip weapon category now can roll both attack and minion modifiers
[*] The Calling Wand weapon category can now exclusively roll minion modifiers
[*] Additional Nightmare mods have been added for the Beastmaster
[/list]

[h2]Chase Uniques[/h2]

Three new chase uniques, part of a set, have been added to the endgame. These do not drop randomly, but are instead hidden somewhere. Can you be the first to finish the set?

[h2]New Items[/h2]

[list]
[*] New item base types have been added for the Arcanist
[*] New uniques have been added for the Arcanist and Beastmaster
[*] New item modifiers have been added for the Arcanist and the Beastmaster
[*] 17 new base types have been added, with more on the way
[/list]


[h2]Balance[/h2]

[list]
[*] Whirlwind's Damage Effectiveness has increased from 60% to 90%. This is a buff
[*] Treasure Beetles no longer share spawn points with other events like Shrines. You will see them substantially more often
[/list]

[h2]Online Features[/h2]

Note that the game does not require you to be online. These are optional Steam features.

[list]
[*] Added the Hall of Heroes, which includes various Steam leaderboards
[*] Added friends list rich presence so you can show off how cool you are for playing this video game
[/list]

[h2]User Interface[/h2]

[list]
[*] Revamped the Character Select screen to not be awful and confusing
[*] Added "The Codex" entry to the Pause screen
[*] Added "Mod Dictionary" to the Codex. This contains a list of every non-unique item modifier in the game, direct from the mod database that creates items
[*] Tooltip positioning has been re-done. Off-screen tooltips should no longer occur. Larger tooltips on items may re-position based on where they're located on the screen as well
[*] Display of Skill tooltips has been improved to be more readable
[*] Item modifiers have had their tier display reversed. The highest tier is now "T1" and the lowest is now "T10". This is purely cosmetic, but makes it obvious when you've found the best possible version of a modifier, since it will always be T1
[*] Added a new option which lets you turn off item/health/mana/exp projectiles ingame. This may improve visibility and performance very lategame
[/list]

[h2]Engine and Performance[/h2]

[list]
[*] A good chunk of the underlying engine has been upgraded. Hopefully this will improve performance, but a lot of testing is required
[*] Shaders now compile more efficiently
[*] Some changes to how controls work have been implemented. You should see no real change here, it's just laying the groundwork for controller rebinding
[*] Improved the handling of save files for very large files
[*] Improved the save file backup system to avoid potential data loss for very large files
[/list]

[h2]Bugfixes[/h2]

[list]
[*] Fixed a bug where the Stats panel was doubling your equipment and skills inappropriately. This was purely cosmetic, but you'll notice lower damage displays on this panel. I promise you did not lose damage, this display was just incorrect
[*] Fixed some damage conversion bugs
[*] Fixed some instances of Area of Effect not functioning
[*] Fixed some instances of Grip of Ascalon not increasing stats
[*] Fixed a bug where some resolutions could not see the Artifact scrollbar
[/list]

notes.title: Endgame Content Update!
notes.content:
Hi everyone, and thanks again for participating in the Don't Die, Collect Loot playtest! I've been over the moon thanks to the outpouring of support and feedback from all of you.

The current playtest has gone really well! That being said, the testing phase will be ending relatively soon. The current build will continue to be playable, but will be converted to a demo (yes, your saves will still be there!) for easier access. I'll still fix bugs on the demo, but major new content won't always make it over to that build.

There will be future playtest builds, likely focused on specific characters and content added over time as I prepare the game to become a more fully-featured release. Players who have actively engaged with the playtest will also receive keys for the Alpha build of the game, where they can continue to play the latest builds even after the testing phase ends. I'll be reaching out to folks directly, but if you're interested drop me a line!

Additionally, there will still be two content patches for the current playtest before it ends, and you're about to read about the first one now! The next patch will focus on the third character, the Arcanist.

[h1]Nightmare Items[/h1]

The main focus of this patch is to add more fun endgame progression in the Nightmare difficulty. While it can be fun to push your character to the limits in the infinite scaling dungeon, it'll be even more exciting if there are actual rewards!

Those rewards have landed in the form of Nightmare items. These items are special rare drops that only appear on Nightmare, and are more likely to appear on higher Nightmare levels, so start farming those boss keys!

Nightmare items always have the maximum amount of modifiers the item can support, usually 5-6 depending on the item. These modifiers have extremely lucky rolls, heavily biasing towards being tier 7-10. They also always include one special modifier unique to Nightmare items, and the base itself is also extremely powerful and unique!

Here are two randomly rolled Nightmare items:

[img]https://i.imgur.com/iduD66X.png[/img]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/s6I2sP1.png[/img]

More Nightmare bases and modifiers will be added in the coming days


[h1]Chaos Bound[/h1]

When these memories were originally sealed and the growth of the world as we know it halted, three incredibly powerful people sealed themselves away within them to ensure nobody would undo their efforts.

Unfortunately for you, they've taken notice of what you're up to and are once again awake. Provoke their ire and you may not live to regret it.

[h1]Other Changes[/h1]
[list]
[*] Added a handful of new unique items
[*] Increased the base scroll speed of the game noticeably
[*] Added a new type of treasure chest only on Nightmare
[*] Made source of "final" damage multiplier more distinct and clear
[*] Nerfed Frozen Slime damage scaling
[*] Buffed the damage of all ranged pets substantially
[*] Added the ability for multiple entities to make up a single boss
[*] Removed the debug menu from the production build
[*] Fixed a bug where not all treasure chest opens were counting for certain achievements
[/list]

notes.title: Major Update - v0.2.2 - Twist of Fate
notes.content:
[h1]Goddess of Fate[/h1]
Whenever you complete an event, the game will no longer automatically create a new stretch of random tiles for you to play through. Instead, the Goddess of Fate will send an avatar in the form of a statue to interact with. You’ll have to use the statue to proceed. When you do, you’ll be presented with a number of choices describing how you’d like the next area to be generated.

An example: 
[img]https://i.imgur.com/6nZvCPi.png[/img]

This new feature gives you a lot more control of what events you’ll see, what features will show up, and what area themes will be selected. There are also rare hidden effects you might find if you get lucky!

[h1]Itemization Changes[/h1]
Items are unsurprisingly at the core of Don’t Die, Collect Loot. Unfortunately, they still weren’t as enjoyable as I was hoping for. This update attempts to address one of the core issues, the fact that you receive too many poor items, especially on long runs.

Starting in 0.2.2, item drops will be somewhat rarer. Depending on how you configure your runs, they’ll be somewhere between 2 and 3 times rarer in most cases. On the upside, they’ll spawn with more modifiers more frequently, and those modifiers will generally be more powerful! In addition, items now support up to 6 total modifiers instead of 4. You’ll rarely see one drop with 5 or 6 mods, but you can fix that with the Crafter.

[h1]Crafter Revamp[/h1]
The Crafter is a crucial part of Don’t Die, Collect Loot. Players who have made it through Inferno difficulty know that she’s essential to creating items necessary to survive. However, despite her power, she was painfully boring. The old crafting process involved finding a good high level item, rerolling it via the Crafter until it had one good modifier, and then having her add a modifier, hoping it would be a good one. This process would then be repeated until a perfect 4-mod item was created.

In v0.2.2, this will no longer work. The Crafter’s abilities in the Nexus have been somewhat reduced. Most notably, you won’t be able to remove modifiers anymore. Additionally, resetting the Chaos value in the Nexus is no longer possible.

Don’t despair though, the Crafter still wants to help out! She’s decided to risk her life and enter the same memories you explore. Encountering her there will result in some extremely powerful crafting possibilities. For example:

[img]https://i.imgur.com/Hv7RWaX.png[/img]

In this image, the Crafter has opted to give the player 3 crafts:

[olist]
[*] All Modifier Tiers +1
[*] Remove Prefix, Add Suffix
[*] Reset Chaos
[/olist]

You’ll also notice that all of these have a 100% chance of succeeding! The downside is that you’ll only be able to pick one, so choose wisely. The Crafter has an extremely powerful pool of modifiers available when you find her like this, and the ones I’ve showed you are on the low end of the power scale. There’s also rumors that she’s been experimenting with a forbidden crafting technique, but you’ll have to ask her about that.

Lastly, you can now craft on equipped items! No more juggling your equipment to make modifications.

[h1]Quest Progression System[/h1]
Don’t Die, Collect Loot has some great progression systems, but a powerful between-run meta progression system that didn’t involve items or skills was missing. To fix that, I’ve added a new Quest system. v0.2.2 adds “General” quests, which serve as a rough roadmap for how to progress through the game. Future updates will include “Class” and “Memory” quests as well.

Completing a quest gives you a permanent reward. “General” quests focus on awarding permanent experience gain rates, along with permanent bonus skill points. Keep an eye on the quest board in town if you want to check in on how you’re progressing. Additionally, these quests are configured such that, in future Steam releases, they’ll also award achievements!

Partially revealed quest board: 
[img]https://i.imgur.com/HydRxcI.png[/img]

[h1]Shopkeeper Event Improvement[/h1]
The Shopkeeper event was generally considered to be a bummer to find. She offered items at a lower price, but the other events were far stronger. To help improve this, the Shopkeeper will now always sell a random unique item. Happy hunting!

[h1]Tooltip Display Formatting[/h1]
Tooltips can get pretty dense in this game, and I’ve heard some players give feedback around them being difficult to read. Starting in v0.2.2, all tooltip text is passed through an auto-formatted that colorizes and bolds specific effects. For example, all “Life” modifiers will be red, regardless of whether they’re found on items, skills, upgrades, or anything else!

[h1]Endgame Content[/h1]
Endgame content is still pretty far down the list, but one new endgame boss has made its way into the game a bit ahead of schedule. I’ll leave it to the more dedicated players to find it and try to survive!

[h1]Update Information[/h1]
The main title screen now includes a quick summary of the current update, and the approximate amount of time until the next major update. Minor updates will still occur now and again, but if you’re interested in major gameplay-altering content, the “Next Update:” display will let you know when to expect it.

[h1]Other Patch Notes[/h1]
[list]
[*] Fixed a bug where Artifacts didn’t apply to players
[*] Reduced the rate at which Shield Toss repeatedly damages enemies
[*] Reduced the rate at which Blade Toss repeatedly damages enemies
[*] Poison-tipped Blades now adds 1 Poison Damage instead of 2 Poison Damage
[*] Added one new endgame boss
[*] Astral Incursions on higher difficulties now have significantly more life
[*] Bosses on higher difficulties now have significantly more life
[*] Monsters on higher difficulties now have slightly higher resistances and base damage
[*] Fixed some bugs with skill tooltips
[*] Fixed some bugs with interacting with Shrines will using a controller
[*] Fixed a level generation bug involving the Crafter ingame event
[*] Removed the item tier display from implicits
[*] Fixed a bug where certain sources of unique items were rewarding uniques of a higher tier than intended
[*] Fixed a bug where Treasure Beetles ran from you at an extremely slow speed
[*] Added 5 new unique items
[*] Fixed some minor bugs
[/list]

[*] Fixed a bug where NPCs would refuse to talk to you in secret areas
[*] Sped up the wave event (Note: This event is likely going to be moved out of Astral Incursions due to how much it interrupts gameplay flow)
[*] Increased the base character move speed by 20%
[/list]
